stories.headline: Lennart Meri Conference 2026 in Tallinn draws regional leaders and shapes European defense debate
stories.summary: The Lennart Meri Conference, Estonia's flagship annual security forum, took place in Tallinn around May 15–17, featuring a keynote by President Karis calling for a militarily capable Europe and hundreds of billions in defense investment. Defence Minister Pevkur warned the conference that European military procurement costs have risen more than 50% in two years due to rearming demand. The forum also hosted diplomatic sideline meetings: PM Michal and President Karis received Albanian PM Rama, President Karis met Moldovan President Sandu and Montenegrin President Milatović.

stories.headline: Kevadtorm 2026 — Estonia's largest annual military exercise mobilizes thousands of reservists and allied forces
stories.summary: Kevadtorm 2026, the Estonian Defence Forces' largest annual exercise, ran from approximately May 10–19, mobilizing thousands of reservists, conscripts, Kaitseliit members, and allied soldiers to practice combined operations and territorial defense. The exercise included drone warfare training for reservists, joint Kaitseliit-police patrols in southern Estonia, and allied heavy equipment deploying to southern Estonia for combat practice.

stories.headline: EKRE parliamentary faction loses non-party MP Vooglaid over foreign and security policy disagreements
stories.summary: Riigikogu MP Varro Vooglaid announced on May 14 that he was leaving the EKRE parliamentary faction, citing loss of leadership trust and deepening disagreements on foreign and security policy, including a dispute over a video in which he called veterans mercenaries. Vooglaid will remain in parliament as an independent; EKRE party chair Martin Helme said Vooglaid was presented with conditions he declined to accept. The departure leaves the Riigikogu with more unaffiliated MPs than at any point this century.

stories.headline: Pevkur calls for accountability on EU's €90 billion Ukraine loan amid corruption probe
stories.summary: Estonian Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur told Euronews there is 'no question' that accountability must be enforced for the EU's €90 billion loan to Ukraine, as a former Zelenskyy aide is investigated for graft. Pevkur said Ukraine's defence minister must demonstrate how funds will be used and that it is Ukraine's responsibility to show all is in order.

stories.headline: Estonia expands South Korean Chunmoo rocket contract — total order rises to nine systems
stories.summary: Estonia signed a contract with Hanwha Aerospace for three additional Chunmoo multiple-launch rocket systems, bringing the total order from six to nine units, with delivery expected by end of 2027. Defence Minister Pevkur called the expansion a significant capability upgrade and highlighted the effectiveness of cooperation with South Korean partners.

stories.headline: Tsahkna urges Europe to pressure weakened Russia, not negotiate; calls for 0.25% GDP Ukraine aid
stories.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna told Bloomberg that Europe should use Russia's weakened position to increase pressure rather than seek negotiations, saying 'now is not the time for talk.' Tsahkna also called on Ramstein coalition countries to follow Estonia's lead and commit 0.25% of GDP annually to Ukraine's military aid, and dismissed Gerhard Schröder as a possible EU-Russia intermediary.

stories.headline: Reform Party general assembly — PM Michal frames 2027 Riigikogu election as contest between freedom and anger
stories.summary: The Reform Party held its general assembly on May 17, at which PM and party chair Kristen Michal delivered a keynote warning of a growing 'conservative octopus' threatening Estonia's freedoms and positioning the 2027 election as a choice between openness and reactionary politics. Party secretary-general Vaga said Reform would contest the election with a clear future vision, and various MPs addressed the congress on pensions, AI investment, and defense.

stories.summary: Eesti Pank announced it will release a specially designed €2 commemorative coin on June 5 dedicated to Sipsik, the beloved Estonian children's book character, to mark the character's 65th anniversary. One million coins have been minted; a concert event at Toompark in Tallinn is planned to coincide with the launch.

stories.headline: Coop Pank posts 51% profit growth in April; Moody's upgrades deposit rating to Baa1
stories.summary: Coop Pank reported April 2026 net profit up 51% year-on-year to €2.8 million, with return on equity at 14%. Moody's simultaneously upgraded the bank's long-term deposit rating from Baa2 to Baa1 with a stable outlook, citing improved reliability. The bank also continued a share buyback programme initiated following an April shareholder decision.

stories.headline: Pevkur advocates stronger NATO eastern flank; Estonia explores Strait of Hormuz deployment
stories.summary: Defence Minister Pevkur joined Baltic and Romanian counterparts in calling for greater EU defense capacity on NATO's eastern flank. Separately, Pevkur said Estonia is exploring participation in a joint French-British mission at the Strait of Hormuz, potentially with staff officers, underwater robots, or a full ship crew. He also weighed in on Latvia's drone incident, saying Ukraine's best remedy is tighter control of its own operations.
